# data - price series. The only tier that cannot be regenerated by us

One job: hold the raw market data the backtester reads. **Nothing here is derived. Nothing here is edited.**

## Drop files here

Databento NQ exports go in `raw/`. Leave them exactly as downloaded - original filename, original format, no cleaning, no re-saving in Excel.

**Why:** every other tier in this workspace can be rebuilt from a script (`transcripts/`, `corpus/_index.md`, `bars/output/`). This one cannot. It is bought data - **append-only, never edited in place.**

## What the model needs

From `../THE-MODEL.md`, the timeframes that actually appear in the corpus:

| timeframe | used for | source |
|---|---|---|
| **1 minute** | entries, the finest cascade step | ep06 [26:35] |
| 2, 3, 4, 5 minute | the cascade - **derivable from 1m** | ep06, ep11, ep12 |
| **15 minute** | the bellwether chart | ep05 [07:06], ep12 [29:00] |
| **1 hour** | frames the trade | ep12 [28:51] |
| **Daily** | bias, draw, order blocks | ep12 [28:47] |
| Weekly | expansion direction | ep40 [21:34] |

**So: 1-minute OHLCV is the only thing strictly required.** Everything above it resamples cleanly. Anything finer (tick, MBP) is optional and only matters if fill realism is later modelled.

## THE TIMEZONE RULE - read this before writing any code

**Every time reference in the entire corpus is New York local time**, and he repeats it in at least six episodes (ep03 [32:59], ep05 [09:03], ep16 [05:32], ep19 [94:41], ep21 [11:26], ep25 [26:07]):

> `always put your chart on New York. I don't care where you live.`

**Databento delivers UTC.** So:

1. Store raw as delivered - UTC, untouched.
2. Convert to **America/New_York** at load time, **with DST**, never with a fixed offset.
3. A fixed -5 or -4 offset silently breaks half the year. ep21 [11:26] addresses this directly: he says set the chart to New York and stop thinking about daylight savings.

**The whole model is a clock.** 8:30, 9:30, 10:00-11:00, noon-1:00, 1:30, 3:00-4:00. Get the timezone wrong and every gate fires at the wrong bar.

## Contract rollover

NQ is quarterly: **H (Mar), M (Jun), U (Sep), Z (Dec)** - ep05 [02:27].

- Expiry: **third Friday** of the delivery month - ep05 [03:12]
- His roll rule: about a week before expiry, switch to whichever month has **larger open interest** - ep05 [04:47]

**A continuous/back-adjusted series is NOT equivalent** for this model. Gaps at the roll matter, because levels are drawn on actual traded prices - previous-day highs, relative equal highs, order blocks. **Prefer individual contract months, and handle the roll explicitly.**

## Layout

```
data/
  CONTEXT.md          <- this file
  raw/                <- Databento files, as downloaded, never edited
  README-<source>.md  <- one note per dataset: what it is, when pulled, what range
```

## Human check

Before trusting any backtest result, verify on **one known day**:

1. Pick a day covered by a `../study/ep<NN>.md` page that quotes exact prices.
2. Load the data, convert to New York time.
3. Confirm the 8:30 and 9:30 bars land where he says, and that the prices he quotes appear.

**ep31 is a good candidate** - entry 4007.75, day's low ~3910, and a stated draw. If those do not line up, the data or the timezone is wrong, and every downstream result is noise.

Do this **before** the first backtest, not after a surprising result.
